extracted.intended_audience: postdoctoral researchers applying for NIA K99/R00 Pathway to Independence awards (and their mentors/administrative staff)
extracted.subtask_description: Preparing and assembling a complete K99/R00 (NIH Pathway to Independence) application including candidate training plan, research strategy, human subjects protections, data safety and monitoring, statistical justification, and institutional/resource documentation for a clinical-trial-required FOA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow FOA/application instructions
rubrics_metrics.description: Always follow your funding opportunity's instructions for application format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although sample applications demonstrate good grantsmanship, time has passed since these grantees applied and the samples may not reflect the latest format or rules; use the FOA's current instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include required application components (table of contents)
rubrics_metrics.description: Application must include SF424 R&R Cover Page, Project Summary/Abstract, Project Narrative, Bibliography & References Cited, Facilities & Other Resources, Equipment, Research & Related Budget (Years 1–5), Budget Justification, PHS398 Career Development Award materials including Candidate Information and Goals, Specific Aims, Research Strategy, Training in Responsible Conduct of Research, Mentor plans, Letters of Support, Institutional Commitment, PHS Human Subjects and Clinical Trials Information, Resource Sharing and Authentication plans, Appendices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the SF424 R&R and PHS-398 specific table of contents ordering and attach named PDF files for required components (e.g., Project Summary.pdf, Project Narrative.pdf).

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Summary/Abstract content and alignment
rubrics_metrics.description: Project Summary/Abstract should state the long-term objective and immediate training goals, list specific training objectives, summarize the research aims, and explain how the proposed project aligns with the institute's mission and strategic goals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly describe both the K99 training phase objectives (e.g., substantive knowledge, intervention development skills, clinical trial design, professional development) and the R00 transition to independence; show institutional support and fit with NIA mission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Narrative (public health relevance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Project Narrative should clearly state the potential to increase understanding and improve clinical care or public health (e.g., improve home hospice care delivery for patients with dementia and their family caregivers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize practical, culturally inclusive interventions and the translational significance of the proposed work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific Aims clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific aims must be enumerated and tied to the training and research plan (e.g., Aim 1 identify challenges/strategies; Aim 2 adapt training materials; Aim 3 test feasibility/acceptability; Aim 4 pilot randomized controlled trial for preliminary efficacy).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each aim should have a clear objective, methods overview, and linkage to overall training/development goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human Subjects indication and IRB status
rubrics_metrics.description: The application must answer whether human subjects are involved, whether the project is exempt, and whether IRB review is pending or approved; include Human Subject Assurance number and IRB approval dates if available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If human subjects are involved and not exempt, indicate IRB review pending or approved and supply assurance numbers; complete PHS Human Subjects and Clinical Trials information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection of Human Subjects justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide rationale that the knowledge to be gained justifies the minimal and reasonable risk to participants; describe anticipated benefits and how risks will be minimized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly discuss potential benefits to subjects and society, and justify risk/benefit balance (e.g., improving dementia care justifies minimal risks).

rubrics_metrics.name: Data Safety and Monitoring Plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe secure storage, access controls, monitoring procedures, frequency of data review, and roles for data oversight (e.g., secure server, password-protected files, weekly and semi-annual reviews, annual IRB review).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include specifics: who reviews consent forms, who records recruitment/enrollment, reporting cadence (weekly reports, semi-annual team reviews), central data storage location, and plan for revising the plan at R00 phase if institution changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adverse Event reporting procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Define how adverse events will be identified, documented, and reported to IRBs and federal agencies, including timelines (e.g., report within 24 hours of discovery) and team communication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State that all adverse events will be discussed with the PI/team and reported per institutional and federal requirements; ensure personnel training in human subjects protections is completed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data monitoring and documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Tracking forms and logs should be used to document reviews, recruitment/enrollment, and data completeness; the PI will review consent forms and entry accuracy regularly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify who generates reports (e.g., research assistant generates weekly enrollment reports) and the schedule for PI review of data entry (e.g., weekly) and team review (e.g., semi-annually).

rubrics_metrics.name: Study team structure and roles
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide names, roles, and institutional affiliations of primary investigators, mentors, co-mentors, site medical directors, and research staff; describe participating sites and recruitment facilitators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain responsibilities (e.g., who facilitates recruitment at sites, who administers protocol) and note that structure may be revised for the R00 institution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protocol synopsis and study design specification
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a brief summary, narrative study description, primary purpose, intervention type/name/description, study phase, intervention model (e.g., parallel), masking, allocation (e.g., randomized), and other design elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly state whether the study meets NIH definitions for clinical trials and whether it is an NIH-defined Phase III trial; list masking levels and allocation method.

rubrics_metrics.name: Randomization and unit of allocation
rubrics_metrics.description: Clearly state how participants/providers/teams will be randomized (e.g., randomize teams of hospice clinicians to intervention or control) and how participants are assigned to groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe clustering, assignment of family caregivers to the clinician's group, and any implications for analysis (e.g., clustering effects).

rubrics_metrics.name: Outcome measures specification
rubrics_metrics.description: Define primary and secondary outcome measures with time frames, instruments, and brief descriptions (e.g., Primary: Family Caregiver Burden assessed with 12-item Zarit at baseline and visits 2–4; Other: Clinician knowledge using revised Dementia Knowledge Assessment Scale; Patient hospice discharge status at 3 and 6 months).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use validated instruments when possible and tailor assessment questions to training content; specify timing and method of ascertainment and verification (e.g., caregiver report verified in electronic records).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of validated measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Employ validated instruments for outcome assessment (e.g., Zarit Caregiver Burden Inventory, Dementia Knowledge Assessment Scale) or justify revisions and provide psychometric rationale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If revising existing scales, describe how they are adapted and validated or provide references for cutoffs and reliability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical design and power justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide statistical design, power calculations, assumptions (variance, alpha, reliability), consideration of clustering (Vif, ICC), detectable effect sizes (Cohen's d), and references for formulae and assumptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For pilot/clinical trial aims, justify sample sizes consistent with pilot study recommendations, describe analytic approach (e.g., mixed models, two-group comparisons), and show calculations for several scenarios (e.g., correlations between waves).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sample size and pilot study rationale
rubrics_metrics.description: Justify clinician and caregiver sample sizes for pilot objectives (e.g., clinicians n=40, caregivers n=160), referencing pilot study conventions and the ability to detect moderate effect sizes with specified power.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide literature references supporting assumptions (e.g., prior studies like REACH) and show what effect sizes would be detectable under given assumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Culturally inclusive recruitment and equity considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Design recruitment strategies to ensure cultural inclusivity and address disparities (e.g., recruit equal numbers of African American and white family caregivers and involve African American individuals at all stages).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe how the design and recruitment support health equity and reduce disparities, and how stakeholder feedback informs intervention adaptation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissemination and ClinicalTrials.gov compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Plan for registering the trial on ClinicalTrials.gov prior to enrolling the first subject and complying with registration, results reporting, and adverse event reporting requirements in accordance with institutional policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify who (e.g., institution CT.gov administrator or PI) will register, maintain, and report, and ensure informed consent documents state the trial posting requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resource sharing and data sharing plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a data sharing plan consistent with NIH and institutional policies: de-identify data prior to release, share aggregate results in publications and presentations, and share de-identified data under confidentiality/data-sharing agreements with commitments to use data for research only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detail types of data to be shared (audio recordings, self-report measures, demographics), security measures (password-protected servers), and agreements (mutual confidentiality, NDAs) and timelines for sharing (after publication/main findings).

rubrics_metrics.name: Privacy, confidentiality, and HIPAA compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe steps to preserve anonymity and protect PHI, including separate linking files (names ↔ study IDs), de-identification procedures, and adherence to the Office for Civil Rights' Privacy Rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain storage location, access restrictions, and plans to return/destroy shared data after analyses per data use agreements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authentication of key biological/chemical resources statement
rubrics_metrics.description: Address authentication of key biological/chemical resources when applicable; if not applicable, state 'Not applicable.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include an explicit plan or statement for authentication consistent with NIH expectations when the project involves such resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appendices and reference documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Include appendices such as reference letters, recruitment materials, detailed statistical documents (e.g., Statistical Design and Power PDF), dissemination plan PDF, inclusion enrollment reports, and other supporting files.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attach key supporting documents as named files in the application and reference them in the relevant sections; ensure letters and institutional commitments are included.
